"It is the mark of an educated mind to be able to entertain a thought without accepting it" - Aristotle

I think it's important to live by this rule. While I don't agree with a lot of opinions, I almost always give the idea a listen through, and to be honest, I've ended up embracing the ideas of some groups that I thought were crazy or just being stupid. It's best to feel yourself growing as a person when someone corrects your or opens your mind to a new idea than to feel embarrassed about being wrong or initially overlooking a great idea.
What if the idea presented to you is something horrible like justifying genocide?
Well I certainly would draw the line there; that's unacceptable and I would call into question the mental stability of the person making these claims.

i think you could use some mind-opening in that case. if there is a rational basis behind the action then it's worth considering the perspective. knee-jerk judgement isn't healthy for clear thinking. do i like genocide? No, but i think it's helpful to understand why and how it occurs if I want to oppose it.

i think you could use some mind-opening in that case.

Yeah, I'm sure the U.S. and those European countries that capitulated to Hitler in WW2 just needed to open their minds and consider a new perspective. After all, who's to say those damn Jews weren't the cause of Germany's decline and that they don't secretly run the world through a secret cabal of Jewish bankers?

Seriously though, people simply couldn't function if they couldn't draw a line where something is absolutely unacceptable or if they couldn't make snap judgements about themselves, others and their environment. We operate on those snap judgements and assumptions every second of every day because the capacity of the human brain is limited and we would suffer information overload if we considered literally every single perspective. It isn't always worth it to do so, in fact sometimes it can be detrimental and distract people from the real issues.
